title: Catenary Pavilion
team: Andrea Cutroni, Flavia Tassi, Alessandra Del Pico
program: University of Rome Tor Vergata — Structures in Architecture
description: A Grasshopper structure inspired by Félix Candela's hypar shells, discretized into a waffle system of optimized catenary arches.
body: Inspired by Félix Candela's Restaurante Los Manantiales, the Catenary Pavilion is a parametric structure whose surface is obtained from the intersection of two hyperbolic paraboloids. The surface is discretized into a waffle structure, with the arches optimized as catenary curves for pure compression behavior.

A 1:1 prototype was realized in MDF using a laser-cutting service, testing the buildability of the parametric geometry and demonstrating how computational form-finding can generate complex, materially efficient shell structures.

sections.title: From Félix Candela to Digital Fabrication
body: The starting point is Candela's Restaurante Los Manantiales — a concrete shell whose geometry comes from intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids. Rebuilt parametrically, that same intersection is discretized into a waffle of interlocking ribs, with each arch optimized as a catenary so the structure works in pure compression.

sections.title: Construction Process
body: Seven assembly steps take the laser-cut MDF ribs from flat parts to the standing shell, each rib slotting into its cross-member without fixings.

sections.title: Prototype
body: The 1:1 prototype, built in MDF through a laser-cutting service — the test of whether the parametric geometry is actually buildable.
